fieldworkDocument.title: Measgaichte / Miscellaneous
fieldworkDocument.note: [NOTES: some notes added (most probably by K. D. MacDonald?). See below for details.]

item.description: a root used for dyeing.
lichen. A dark, grey colour obtained from this.
a light grey colour was obtained from the root of the iris.
spindle. For winding thread.
the long platform where wool was waulked. It had a rounded head. [NOTES: note added above ‘cliabh’ – from cliath?]
this phrase indicated that the wool had been wrapped round this wooden hogshead (còrn). This was done after waulking.
this was the measurement by which the wool had to contract during waulking. Approx. the length of the middle finger.
the kiln wall. About three feet high and ten feet wide.
the part of the kiln where the seed was placed to dry.
a sheep’s skin.
the water powered wheel in a mill.
little white eddies on the sea surface. Indicating gales and high winds.
seals squealing. A sign of bad weather. [NOTES: ‘cabraid’ corrected to ‘càbraid’.]
a language unto themselves. Reference to previous word.
louping ill. Caused by a tick with a red head. The other four types of tick are not so dangerous.
embers.

the skin which is taken off a dead calf or lamb and placed on another so as to endear it to its new mother. Also called a ‘luairceinn’. [NOTES: ‘laoghachcainn’ corrected to ‘laoghachcain’ and ‘luairceinn’ to ‘luaircein’.]
balsam. [NOTES: ‘òla’ corrected to ‘ola’.]
general term for an earmark.
a rope between two ploughing horses.
a small circle in which a hook can be placed.
the bit in a horse’s mouth.
tools.
fidgety.
a bit of wood which was placed on an animal’s face to prevent them from fighting. Had nails on the inside of the wood to act as a deterrent. [NOTES: corrected to ‘bùireasg’.]
a saddle with baskets attached. [NOTES: ‘chleibh’ corrected to ‘chlèibh’.]
these were the parts of the saddle where the baskets rested.
a plaid underneath the saddle which prevented the baskets from cutting the skin.
a twitch used for controlling a horse when it was being shod. Made of a wooden handle with a rope at one end attached to the horse’s face. When it was twisted, it tightened so as to hurt the horse.
